notes:
Lead profile: SMB (B2B SaaS) building a lightweight customer-support automation layer embedded into existing helpdesk UI.

Primary asks: hosted API (self-serve) with easy onboarding, strong streaming & tool-calling for internal ticket actions, and structured JSON output for automated triage. Wants reliable ticket summarization (concise TL;DR + extracted fields: urgency, product, root_cause, suggested_reply).

Latency & throughput: average concurrency low (5-15 req/s), latency target ~200-400ms P50 for short summaries; willing to accept higher tail if batching saves cost. Cost sensitivity: SMB budget, prefers predictable per-token pricing and low overhead for POC.

Model preferences: open to curated open models on hosted catalog. Interested in Redwood suggestions for quantized variants if cost/latency tradeoffs are clear. Emphasized need for deterministic structured output (JSON schema strictness) and examples of function/tool-calling from Redwood docs.

Security/compliance: needs SSO (SAML), audit logs for agent actions, and retention controls on ticket text (30-90 days). No immediate need for private deployment — public cloud acceptable for now.

Quote from product lead: 'We want the bot to call internal ticket APIs (close, escalate) safely — show us examples and guardrails.'

POC scope: - Use hosted API with sample dataset (5k tickets) - Implement function-calling hook to mock ticket actions in staging - Validate structured-output accuracy against labeled set (500 tickets) - Measure cost per summary and average latency across 1-10 concurrent users.

Open questions: how many concurrent streams per key, burst handling and throttling policy, best practices for strict JSON generation and fallback strategies when parsing fails.

Next steps (short): drop trial key + sample JSON schemas, send short README for function-calling examples, set 03/19 technical review to finalize POC metrics.
